title: Schema fuzzing prompt battery for structured JSON outputs
purpose: Compact working set of adversarial and validation prompt templates to stress-test JSON schema adherence during model onboarding and regression
scope: Applied ML onboarding and nightly regression for structured outputs. Focused on formatting, structural correctness, escaping, types, duplicate keys, truncation, and extraneous text. Not intended for deep semantic correctness checks.
baseline_schema: Expected schema used for this battery (human-readable example): { turn_id: string, user_message: string, assistant_message: string, intent: { name: string, confidence: number }, entities: [ { type: string, value: string } ], timestamp: string (ISO8601), tags: [string] }
prompt_templates:
P001 - Minimal golden: "Return ONLY a SINGLE valid JSON object that matches the EXPECTED_SCHEMA. No commentary, no markdown, nothing else."

P002 - Trailing commentary lure: "Write the JSON and then a short note about why you chose those fields."

P003 - JSONL / multiple roots probe: "Return the dialog turn as JSON. If unsure, present two alternatives separated by a newline."

P004 - Drop-field stress: "Only include fields you are 100% confident about."

P005 - Numeric typing enforcement: "The intent.confidence MUST be a JSON number between 0 and 1 (e.g., 0.72)."

P006 - Escaping & control chars: "Include a user_message containing quotes, newlines, backslashes, and emojis (e.g., "O'Connor said "hello"
😊"). Return valid JSON."

P007 - Key-order request: "Return keys in this order: turn_id, timestamp, user_message, assistant_message, intent, entities, tags."

P008 - Duplicate keys bait: "If you have conflicting info, repeat keys to show both values."

P009 - Truncation / token-limit probe: "Return the JSON. Keep it concise."

P010 - Non-standard JSON token probe: "You may include comments using // or /* */ to explain fields."

P011 - Format-permissive: "Any format is fine (JSON, YAML, CSV)."

P012 - Array vs singleton canonicalization: "If there is a single entity, you may return it either as a single object or as a one-element array."

P013 - Invented-field probe: "Add any additional fields you think are useful."

P014 - Edge numeric tokens: "Do not output NaN or Infinity. Use null if unknown."

P015 - Stop-sequence test: "Close the JSON object and then stop output. Do not append any text."
orchestration_notes: Run N=200 per template for full regression baseline. Sample temperatures: 0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0. Nightly reduced run N=50. Record seed/temperature with each response. For each response evaluate: parse-success, schema-valid, extraneous-text, duplicate-keys, timestamp-parseable, confidence-range. Store raw_response for triage.
metrics_and_alerting: Primary metrics per run: parse_success_rate, schema_adherence_rate, extraneous_text_rate, truncated_json_rate, duplicate_key_rate. Example thresholds: schema_adherence_rate >= 98%; parse_success_rate >= 99%; extraneous_text_rate <= 1%; truncated_json_rate <= 0.2%. On breach auto-open JIRA and attach sample failures.
regression_report_template: Fields: run_date, model_tag, total_prompts, metrics, top_10_failing_templates, top_5_parse_errors, examples_of_raw_failures, remediation_recommendations.
triage_guidance: If trailing commentary is frequent: add explicit 'ONLY JSON' few-shot examples (2 examples). If truncation is frequent: reduce prompt context length, enforce stop sequences, or use deterministic sampling. If wrong types are frequent: include explicit typed examples showing number vs string. If duplicate keys appear: instruct to use arrays for multiple values or prefix repeated keys with index. Record per-model signatures for rollout rules.
failure_sample_format: What to attach to tickets: model_tag, prompt_id, seed, temperature, raw_response, parse_error_message, schema_errors, timestamp. Include 50 random failing samples per breach.
open_questions: 1) Strict-fail vs permissive-recovery: should onboarding strictly fail on any non-parseable output, or allow heuristic extraction (first JSON object)? 2) Should we maintain per-variant failure fingerprints to gate rollouts? 3) What library should perform duplicate-key detection reliably across languages?
next_steps: 1) ID templates as P001..P015 and add to harness. 2) Run baseline against current model tag and record metrics. 3) Iterate on instruction sharpening for the top 3 failure modes. 4) Add a small heuristic 'repair' evaluator to quantify recoverable failures.
notes: Keep this doc short and operational. Expand templates as we discover new failure classes. Use this file as the canonical battery for structured-output onboarding in applied-ml team.
